overall_reason: The header marks 'Home' as the current page and 'Add to compare' answers at once (the plus turns to a check and the header Compare button gains a count badge), but the header shows 'Compare' twice, the compare control is a bare plus icon, and the stylesheet declares no pressed state.

score.reason: T-WHERE-AM-I passes and the async run shows designed feedback on 'Add to compare', with gaps in T-ONE-FAMILY and T-WHERE-AM-I (a duplicated 'Compare' destination, CMP-150), T-STATE-MATRIX (no :active rule, CMP-002) and T-INTERRUPT (the 'Made in Bolt' pill, CMP-183).

visitor_mode: Persuade with a light Operate layer (a tool picker plus a compare tray). No 00-contract.md; inferred from the hero 'Tell us the goal. We'll build the stack.' and the per-card compare controls.

findings.title: Decide and name the nav
findings.evidence: The header lists 'Compare' as a nav link and again as a bordered button with a swap icon at the right end ('Compare', which gains the badge '1' in async/a0-slow-final.png). Two controls with the same word sit 200px apart.
findings.before: Two 'Compare' items in one header: a nav link and a tray button.
findings.after: One item: the tray button labelled 'Compare (1)' that opens the comparison, and the nav link removed, or the nav link kept and the tray named 'Your shortlist'.
findings.why: A visitor cannot tell whether the two Compare items go to the same place or whether the link shows the tools they picked.

findings.title: Every state a control can reach is designed
findings.evidence: declared_states reads 315 readable rules with 0 :active rules, 1 :focus-visible rule and 0 hover media queries; the 15 hover rules apply on touch screens too. The buttons table lists four variants on one 8px radius.
findings.before: Buttons have a hover look but no pressed look, and hover is not limited to pointers that hover.
findings.after: A pressed state one step darker or 1px lower on each variant, and hover rules inside @media (hover: hover) (CMP-103, CMP-105).
findings.why: A press gives no feedback until the result arrives, and phone taps leave a sticky hover look.

findings.title: Icon-only buttons expose an accessible name
findings.where: 'Add to compare' plus icon on each tool card, 1440, tiles/1440-02.png
findings.evidence: The buttons table lists 6 icon-only 'Add to compare' buttons, 27px tall, drawn as a bare '+' beside the outlined 'Details' button. The control_names sweep finds them named, so the name exists only for assistive tech; sighted visitors see a plus with no word.
findings.before: A bare plus next to 'Details', with no visible word.
findings.after: A text button 'Compare' with the plus, or a checkbox labelled 'Compare' that shows its checked state.
findings.why: A plus on a tool card reads as 'add to cart' or 'add to my stack'; nothing on the card says it builds a comparison.

findings.title: No popups, newsletter modals, chat bubbles, help pills
findings.where: fixed 'Made in Bolt' pill, bottom right, 1440 and 375, fold-1440.png and fold-375.png
findings.evidence: A fixed white pill 'Made in Bolt' with a close button sits over the bottom-right corner; at 375 it covers the head of the next section ('What are you trying to...').
findings.before: The builder platform's badge floats over content on every screen.
findings.after: Remove the platform badge from the published site.
findings.why: It covers page content without being asked for.

findings.title: The phone gets the whole navigation
findings.evidence: phone_nav records one 'Toggle menu' button (38x38) and only the logo visible at 375; the header Compare button with its count badge is gone at this width, so the only sign that a tool was added is the plus turning into a check.
findings.before: At 375 the compare count is hidden behind an icon-only menu button.
findings.after: The compare count kept in the 375 header beside a 'Menu' button with a visible word and a 44px box.
findings.why: A phone visitor who adds tools to compare cannot see how many they have or reach the comparison without opening the menu.

strengths: The header marks the current page with a filled pale-blue 'Home' pill (fold-1440.png).
'Add to compare' answers within 0.5s: the plus becomes a check on a blue tint and the header Compare button gains a '1' badge (async/a0-slow-0.5s.png, a0-slow-final.png).
One filled primary per screen: the hero 'Find my stack' beside an outlined 'Browse all tools', and one 'Get started' in the closing band (tiles/1440-02.png).
A skip link is the first focus stop.
not_investigated: The stack-builder flow and the compare page: the captured actions made no same-origin request, so no fail run was possible.
What the phone menu holds and how it opens and closes: the capture opens triggers at 1440 only.
Inline validation and error placement: no fields on the page.
Focus moving into an overlay and back, scroll lock and backdrop click: nothing opened as an overlay.
Keyboard operation of custom widgets: lens-a11y.
The table reads nav_with_current_mark 0, but the screenshot shows the 'Home' pill; I judged from the screenshot.
T-FIELD-READ, T-ERROR-PATH, T-OVERLAY-CHECK, T-FIRST-RUN: no fields, no failure run, no overlay and no onboarding on the page.
